_readme: Self-correction knowledge base (owner-curated). Each entry records a claim
the analysis once made that turned out to be WRONG, with the authoritative
correction. Entries are enforced two ways:
1. DETERMINISTIC — DomainCorrectionsService.enforce() runs at the
synthesis flip and strips/repairs any condition matching an entry's
`match` + `action`, no matter which lane (rules engine or LLM)
asserted it. This is the guarantee.
2. PROMPT — every entry's `correction` text is rendered into the
identify + verification prompts so the model stops making the claim
up front. This is the optimization.
Add entries when feedback (owner or user chat) disproves an analysis
claim. Keep them narrow and factual; cite authority. The file is
deliberately in-repo — it is part of the transparency log.
match fields: name_pattern / basis_pattern are case-insensitive regex,
matched against IdentifiedCondition.name / .presumptiveBasis. A BLANK
stored basis counts as matching (an unexplained presumptive assertion
cannot stand against a name-matched correction); conditions whose name
contains 'undiagnosed' are never stripped (different claim).
actions: strip_presumptive — clear is_presumptive/basis and rewrite the
nexus leg back to needs-direct-connection with the correction noted.

corrections.title: Diagnosed migraines are not a Gulf War presumptive
corrections.wrong_claim: Migraine Headaches (VASRD 8100) presumptively service-connected under Gulf War / 38 CFR 3.317
corrections.correction: 38 CFR 3.317 Gulf War presumptions cover UNDIAGNOSED illnesses and medically unexplained chronic multisymptom illnesses (chronic fatigue syndrome, fibromyalgia, functional GI disorders). Headache is only a sign/symptom of such an undiagnosed illness. Once headaches are DIAGNOSED as a known clinical condition (e.g. Migraine Headaches), the 3.317 presumption does not apply — service connection requires the standard triad (diagnosis, in-service event, nexus) or a secondary theory (e.g. secondary to PTSD or tinnitus). Migraines are also not on any PACT Act presumptive list.

corrections.title: Diagnosed sleep apnea is not a Gulf War presumptive
corrections.wrong_claim: Obstructive Sleep Apnea (VASRD 6847) presumptively service-connected under Gulf War via the 'sleep disturbances' sign/symptom lane
corrections.correction: The 38 CFR 3.317 'sleep disturbances' lane covers signs/symptoms of an UNDIAGNOSED illness. Obstructive Sleep Apnea is a diagnosed condition with a known pathophysiology and is not a Gulf War (or PACT Act) presumptive. Service connection requires the standard triad — commonly an in-service onset shown by lay/buddy evidence plus a nexus opinion, or a secondary theory (e.g. secondary to rhinitis/deviated septum or weight gain from an SC condition).
corrections.authority: 38 CFR 3.317(a)(2)(i); no OSA entry on 3.317/3.320 or PACT lists
